subject: Performance SLO qualification — FinCo latency & context window follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification — FinCo latency & context window follow-up

Alex / Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned on the performance constraints you described and what we need to validate on our side.

Recap of FinCo targets / constraints:
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for short responses (<= 256 output tokens) and <= 800ms for long-form outputs (up to 2048 output tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 120 qps at peak with spikes to 220 qps for short chat messages.
- Concurrency: up to 800 concurrent sessions during daily peak.
- Streaming: Yes — low-latency token streaming is required for the chat UI.
- Context window: input contexts typically range 2k-6k tokens (system + convo + doc snippets). Max single-request input occasionally hits ~12k tokens when including long doc excerpts.
- Output token limits: typically 128–512 tokens, occasionally 2k for long summaries.

Key performance/qualification questions we flagged on the call:
1) Can you share representative payloads (system prompt + worst-case user context + expected output) for short and long flows?
2) For the 12k token worst-case inputs, are you flexible about pre-filtering/summary (chunk & reference pattern), or do you need full context kept as-is?
3) Is streaming mandatory for ALL chat flows, or only interactive user-facing chat?

What we’ll do next (internal validation plan):
- Run workload-shaped microbenchmarks with matching context sizes (short: <=512 tokens, medium: 2k–6k, and worst-case 12k) to measure p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- Test continuous streaming (server push) vs non-streaming modes to measure added latency for first-token and tail completion.
- Explore options: shorter pinned context + external doc store references, KV cache for repeated context, and quantized model variants to meet 250ms SLO for short responses.

Deliverables and timeline:
- I’ll share a benchmarking plan and the SLO matrix today (attachment).
- We’ll aim to have initial benchmark numbers for short/medium contexts by Tue (2026-05-12) and worst-case 12k runs by Thursday (2026-05-14).

Attachments: finco_slo_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLO grid), sample_payloads.json (please confirm these match production shapes).

Next steps for you: please confirm if the sample_payloads represent production shapes and clarify whether full 12k contexts are non-negotiable. Also, if you have concurrency/connection pooling constraints on the client side (websocket limits, connection TTLs), share that so we can simulate correctly.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 250ms SLO is for the chat UI where users expect near-instant replies (these are the short flows, usually <= 128 output tokens). We can accept slightly higher p99 (up to ~400ms) for the short flow if p95 is solid.
- For the 12k inputs: these come from batch analyst workflows where they paste large docs; they don’t require streaming, but must finish within 10s. So for worst-case, streaming is not required.
- Streaming is required for the interactive chat experience only. We have two categories: interactive (real-time, streaming) and batch (long context, non-streaming, 10s cutoff).
- Concurrency: 800 concurrent sessions is peak for EU + US; we may route EU traffic to a regional deployment. We’ll confirm exact regional split next week.

Attached: an anonymized sample payload set (I uploaded to the drive link you included). Also flagging that our internal websocket timeout is 60s; connection reuse may be limited to 6 per process.

We’re flexible on pre-filtering for the 12k use case; if you can implement a safe summarization/embedding-based retrieval pattern that preserves the critical facts, that’s acceptable.

—Alex

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — FinCo latency & context window follow-up

Adding engineering notes from our quick sync:

1) Context window & tokenization impact:
- 12k tokens (worst-case) is expensive: memory and KV-cache churn will increase per-request latency and reduce effective throughput. For autoregressive models, cost ~ O(seq_len * generated_len) per forward pass for attention; long inputs also increase decoding time per step if the runtime must re-attenuate over full context.
- Practical approach: if FinCo can accept retrieval + summarization, we can limit live attention to a 4–6k active window and keep longer context in an indexed store (embeddings + retriever). That typically reduces p95 by 30–60% for typical long queries.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming latency implications:
- Streaming adds negligible per-token delay if we can push tokens as they’re produced, but first-byte latency depends on model chunking and whether we run prefix-only or full attention. For short outputs (<=128 tokens) streaming first-byte can be under 80ms on optimized runtime + quantized model on A100/V100-equivalent instances.
- For long outputs or long input contexts, first-token latency can spike because the encoder pass (attention over 6k+ tokens) must complete before generation. We can pipeline (partial attention + incremental KV) to reduce this, but it’s an implementation tradeoff.

3) Concurrency & batching tradeoffs:
- Achieving 120–220 qps with 800 concurrent sessions will require a mix of batching for throughput and tail-latency controls (priority queues or fast-path) for short interactive messages.
- We’ll test continuous batching policy configs: small-window high-priority fast-path (for short messages) vs larger batch for long-form to maximize throughput. Expect tunable 20–40% differences in cost/throughput depending on config.

4) Model/quantization options:
- To hit 250ms p95 for short flows we recommend testing a quantized 8-bit variant and a distilled small-medium model for the interactive path, with full large model for long/batch runs.

Requests for benchmark run:
- Please confirm sample payloads for: short interactive (<=512 total tokens), medium convo (2k–6k), worst-case (12k input, non-streaming, 2k output).
- If you can provide 1 minute of production traffic capture (anonymized) or a distribution, that helps us shape batching windows.

I’ll draft a benchmark config and expected metrics to collect (p50/p95/p99 first-byte, per-token throughput, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens) and share by EOD.

—Dylan
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
